title: Wire MCP tools into chat with streaming reasoning
description: Extend the existing chat_service/websocket flow to give the LLM access to the MCP tools, streaming its intermediate reasoning and tool calls back over the websocket as it thinks, and include a download link in the final message when the result is tabular.
acceptance_criteria: Asking 'What is the average age of men in South America' over the chat websocket streams incremental messages before the final PII-free answer.

title: MCP server: filter and aggregate tools
description: Expose MCP tools backed by people_service: list_countries, query (exact-match on a country or array of countries, and/or age > / < comparisons, optional gender), and aggregate (average/percentile/bucket queries). Tool schemas and responses are data-efficient (only requested fields/aggregates returned) and never define or return name/ssn/address fields.
acceptance_criteria: Each MCP tool call returns only the requested, PII-free data; combined filters (country + age comparison) work in a single call rather than requiring multiple round trips.

title: PII-safe query + aggregation service
description: app/schemas/people.py: PersonRecord schema exposing only country/age/gender (never name/ssn/address). app/services/people_service.py: list_countries(), filter(countries|region, age_min, age_max, gender), and aggregate(metric: average|percentile|bucket_count, field, group_by, filters) covering: average age of men in South America; age range below the 90th percentile; count of women by 25/50/75/100th percentile buckets.
acceptance_criteria: Service methods return correct results against the fixture CSV for all three example questions in docs/requirements/chat.md; no returned object contains name/ssn/address, even under crafted field-selection input.

title: Country-to-region reference data + lookup
description: Add a country->region (continent) mapping (e.g. app/data/regions.json) and a lookup helper so queries can resolve a region name like 'South America' to its set of countries. Needed because the CSV only has a 'country' column, but example questions filter by region.
acceptance_criteria: Looking up 'South America' returns the expected set of South American countries present in the fixture data; unknown region raises a clear error.

title: CSV data loading + repository layer
description: Add a sample fixture CSV (name, ssn, address, country, age, gender) and app/repositories/people_repository.py that loads it once into memory (no database, per project convention) and exposes the raw rows only internally. Nothing outside the repository may read name/ssn/address.
acceptance_criteria: Repository loads every row from the fixture CSV; a unit test asserts the loaded record count and that the repository's public accessors never return name/ssn/address keys.

title: Stimulus.js chat controller
description: Add a Stimulus.js controller (static/js/controllers/chat_controller.js) wired to the chat page: opens the websocket connection, sends the typed message on submit, and appends incoming messages to the message list in the DOM.
acceptance_criteria: Typing 'Hello RWS' and submitting sends it over the websocket and the 'Hi there' reply is appended to the page without a reload.
close_reason: Stimulus controller connects the websocket, sends on submit, appends replies without reload; verified in browser

title: WebSocket chat endpoint + chat service
description: Add a WebSocket route (in routers/chat.py) that delegates to services/chat_service.py. Router stays thin; business logic (currently: always respond 'Hi there') lives in the service layer.
acceptance_criteria: Connecting to the websocket and sending 'Hello RWS' returns the response 'Hi there'.
close_reason: WebSocket /ws/chat delegates to ChatService.get_response, returns 'Hi there'

title: Chat page route (GET /)
description: Add a thin router (routers/chat.py) exposing GET / that renders templates/chat.html (extends base layout) with the chat UI shell. No authentication required.
acceptance_criteria: Browsing to / returns 200 with the chat page on a light grey background, no login required.
close_reason: GET / renders chat.html via thin router, no auth required

title: Tailwind CSS setup + base HTML layout
description: Add Tailwind CSS (CDN acceptable for this scope) and a base Jinja2 layout template (templates/base.html) with a light grey page background, to be extended by the chat page.
acceptance_criteria: Base layout renders with Tailwind classes applied and a light grey (bg-gray-100 or similar) background.
close_reason: Base Jinja2 layout added with Tailwind CDN and bg-gray-100 background

title: Scaffold FastAPI project structure
description: Set up the app skeleton per CLAUDE.md conventions: app/main.py (app factory, middleware, startup/shutdown), app/config.py (pydantic-settings reading .env), app/dependencies.py, empty routers/ and services/ packages, static/ and templates/ directories. Add pyproject/requirements with fastapi, uvicorn, websockets, jinja2, pydantic-settings, pytest, httpx, ruff, mypy. Configure ruff + mypy.
acceptance_criteria: uvicorn app.main:app --reload starts a working (empty) FastAPI app; ruff check . and mypy app/ pass.
close_reason: FastAPI scaffold in place; app imports, ruff and mypy pass

title: Integration tests incl. PII-leakage guards
description: End-to-end tests covering the three example questions from docs/requirements/chat.md (average age of men in South America; age range below 90th percentile; women counts by quartile) driven through the chat websocket, plus explicit assertions that no response, MCP tool schema, or log ever contains the fixture's name/ssn/address values.
acceptance_criteria: pytest passes for all three example questions end-to-end, and PII-leakage assertions pass across MCP tool outputs and websocket responses.

title: Downloadable CSV export for tabular results
description: Add a thin FastAPI route (e.g. GET /downloads/{export_id}) backed by an export service that turns a tabular query/aggregate result into a downloadable CSV, keyed by an export_id returned from the service layer. No PII fields are ever included in an export.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tabular result (e.g. the quartile-bucketed counts of women), GET /downloads/{export_id} returns a CSV attachment matching exactly the PII-free result rows.

title: MCP CSV query tool: PII-safe, token-efficient data queries
description: Implement the MCP tool defined in docs/requirements/chat.md: lets the chat LLM query a CSV of people (name, ssn, address, country, age, gender) without ever seeing name/ssn/address, using data-efficient filter and aggregate queries. Reasoning streams back to the user over the existing chat websocket; tabular results are downloadable.

title: Integration tests for chat page and websocket
description: Add tests/test_routers/test_chat.py using httpx.AsyncClient: GET / returns 200 with expected chat page content; websocket test sends 'Hello RWS' and asserts the 'Hi there' response.
acceptance_criteria: pytest passes, covering the GET / route and the websocket request/response flow.
close_reason: Added integration tests for GET / and websocket chat flow; pytest, ruff, mypy all pass

title: Chat bubble styling
description: Style rendered messages with Tailwind: user messages as a green bubble, 2/3 page width, right-aligned; responses as a white bubble, 2/3 page width, left-aligned, appearing beneath the corresponding user message.
acceptance_criteria: Typing 'Hello RWS' shows a green 2/3-width right-aligned bubble with the question, and a white 2/3-width left-aligned bubble beneath it with 'Hi there'.
close_reason: Verified in browser: green 2/3-width right-aligned question bubble, white 2/3-width left-aligned response bubble beneath

title: Chat app: FastAPI + WebSocket chat interface
description: Implement the chat web app defined in docs/requirements/framework.md: a FastAPI backend serving a chat HTML page and a WebSocket endpoint, styled with Tailwind CSS and wired up with Stimulus.js on the frontend. No auth, no database.
close_reason: Chat app implemented end-to-end per docs/requirements/framework.md; verified in browser and via pytest
